tldr: The paper introduces openCHA, an open-source LLM-powered framework for Conversational Health Agents that integrates external data sources, knowledge bases, and analysis models to enable multi-step problem-solving, personalized conversations, and multimodal data analysis for healthcare applications.
contributions: Proposes an LLM-powered Orchestrator that acts as a problem solver to address healthcare queries by planning and executing actions
Integrates external healthcare data sources, knowledge bases, and AI/analysis models for reliable, up-to-date responses
Incorporates multimodal and multilingual capabilities into the framework
Demonstrates framework effectiveness through two demos and four use cases
Releases the framework as open source on GitHub
methods: The authors designed openCHA with three major components: an Interface (mobile, desktop, web apps with multimodal communication), an Orchestrator (the core agent with Task Planner, Task Executor, Data Pipe, Promptist, and Response Generator sub-components), and External Sources (APIs for healthcare data, knowledge bases, AI/analysis models). The Task Planner uses Tree of Thought and ReAct prompting methods to decompose queries into sequential tasks, while the Task Executor interacts with external sources and manages intermediate data through the Data Pipe. The Response Generator synthesizes gathered information into personalized, empathetic responses.
results: The framework was demonstrated through two demos and four use cases showing proficiency in handling complex healthcare tasks. The paper highlights capabilities in knowledge acquisition, problem-solving, multilingual and multimodal conversations, and integration with various AI platforms. Specific quantitative results and numerical metrics are not provided in the available text.
limitations: The framework is described as an 'initial iteration' with the aim to 'lay the foundation for developing more sophisticated tools as our journey unfolds,' indicating it is a work in progress. The paper notes that existing LLM-based CHAs struggle with hallucination, outdated information, and lack of multi-step problem-solving—challenges the framework aims to address but which may still require further refinement. Limited quantitative evaluation results are presented in the available text.
